why: TARGET (Century Communities) is a national US homebuilder selling single-family homes, townhomes, condos and paired homes directly to residential buyers (entry-level, first-time, move-up), with affiliated mortgage (Inspire Home Loans), title (Parkway Title) and insurance (IHL) services, operating in 16 states via on-site sales staff, online channels and third-party brokers [T:P1.7, T:P2.2, T:P2.4, T:P2.5, T:P2.6, T:P2.7, T:P3.1]. COMP (Dream Finders Homes) is likewise a US homebuilder selling new construction homes to residential buyers, with on-community sales staff and affiliated financial services, emphasising customer personalisation and service [C:P1.1, C:P1.2, C:P1.5, C:P1.13, C:P2.3]. Both companies build and sell the same types of residential homes to the same B2C buyer segments, with identical ancillary mortgage/title/insurance services — a textbook direct competitor relationship.
reason: Both are US homebuilders selling new-construction single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums directly to entry-level and move-up residential buyers, with affiliated mortgage, title and insurance services. Same product, same customer.

primary_products.reason: Both sell new-construction single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums to residential buyers.

primary_services.reason: Both offer affiliated mortgage financing, title and insurance services to their homebuyers.

customer_segment.reason: Both target B2C residential homebuyers, including first-time and move-up buyers purchasing a new home.

end_markets.reason: Both operate exclusively in US residential new-home construction.

business_model.reason: Both are homebuilder/OEM operators that acquire land, build homes using subcontractors and sell directly to end buyers, with affiliated financial services subsidiaries.

revenue_model.reason: Both earn revenue primarily from home sale closings, supplemented by mortgage origination, title and insurance service fees.

value_chain_position.reason: Both sit at the OEM/developer-to-consumer end of the value chain: land acquisition → construction → direct sale to homebuyer.

geography_served.reason: Century operates across 16 states coast-to-coast; Dream Finders is described as a national builder. Both cover overlapping US Sun Belt and Southeast markets. Century's footprint appears somewhat broader, but both are multi-state US operators.

specialization.reason: Both are specialised residential homebuilders with the same affiliated financial-services model (mortgage + title + insurance) layered on top.

distribution_channels.reason: Both sell through on-site community sales staff/model homes, online channels, and third-party real estate brokers.

regulatory_exposure.reason: Both face the same regulatory environment: zoning/land use/building codes for homebuilding and CFPB/RESPA mortgage-lending rules for their financial services arms.
